description: A rough grey iron ingot from the cupola. The foundry's own heavy-alloy feedstock; also traded to the Railway Restoration Corps and the Valley General Council.
A cast iron plowshare and moldboard. Agricultural continuity: the Botanical Seed Trust and the Valley farms trade food for these.
A forty-kilo structural T-beam. The bone of the bunker's sky-layer armor frames and the station's load-bearing repairs.
Forged rail spikes, counted by the bundle. A treaty obligation to the Railway Restoration Corps — the narrow-gauge line dies without them.
A cast rail-car wheel, chilled and machined at the rim. Heavy, hard, and owed in quotas to the railway charter.
A lead-antimony acid-resistant pipe and valve body, cast for Station 0 Chemical Combine. The Acid Gorge treaty exchanges these for sulfur.
A bolted repair plate for bunker bulkheads, blast doors, and the sky-layer armor grid. Shelter resilience in a flat rectangle of iron.
Cast brackets and threaded fasteners. The quiet hardware that holds piping, shelving, and machinery to the walls.
A cast valve body for the water system — brine, feedwater, and the acid lines. The hydro systems run on these.
A heavy wrench, drift, or sledging bar from the foundry floor. Improves repair and maintenance work across the shelter.
A precision heavy-alloy part — a bearing sleeve, a gear blank, a tuyere boss. The most expensive thing the foundry makes, and the one nobody has spare.
A thickened armor plate for the blast doors and hatch surrounds. Defensive only where the structure demands it; the foundry does not run a weapons line.
Clay-bonded casting sand, wetted and sieved. The mold bed is the foundry's second furnace: it decides whether a casting is clean or cracked.
High-alumina firebrick for the lining and hearth. Scarce, and the difference between a furnace that holds iron and a furnace that kills people.
Crushed limestone flux. It pulls sulfur and slag out of the melt — without it, the iron is brittle and the air is poison.
A bag of lead-antimony shot for the acid-resistant alloy. Station 0 bartered the antimony under the Acid Gorge treaty; the sulfur flows because these pipes hold.
